inputFields.description:
Keep only items of this kind.

Overrides `depth`, because naming a kind is already a statement about depth: asking
for episodes and getting nothing because episodes have parents would be obtuse.

inputFields.description: How deep to look. Defaults to the library's top level.

inputFields.description: Keep only items released in or after this year.

inputFields.description: Keep only items released in or before this year.

inputFields.name: contentRating
inputFields.description:
Keep only items with exactly this age-rating label, as the metadata source expresses
it — for example `fr/Tous publics`. Not comparable across countries.

inputFields.name: studioContains
inputFields.description:
Keep only items whose studio contains this text, case-insensitively.

A substring rather than a name, which is what a caller typing "HBO" means and what
the Plex surface does. It cannot use an index — a leading wildcard has nothing to
seek to — so it is applied after the library predicate and its cost is bounded by
the library, not the table.

inputFields.name: titleWordPrefix
inputFields.description:
Keep only items having a word that starts with this text.

Matches the title, the sort title and the original title, with accents folded: `le`
finds both "Le Nouveau Jouet" and "Sans Laisser de Traces". A word prefix rather than
full-text search, because full-text indexing is the least portable feature across
database engines and the engine is meant to stay swappable.

inputFields.name: minWidth
inputFields.description:
Keep only items with a version at least this wide, in pixels — 3840 for 4K.

The one filter that reaches past the item table, so the one that can slow a listing.

inputFields.name: tags
inputFields.description: Keep only items carrying the named tags. Every condition must hold.

inputFields.name: excludedId
inputFields.description: Leave out this item, as returned in `id`: "the rest of this director's films".

types.name: ItemOrder
types.description:
How a library listing is ordered.

An enum rather than a string because the value becomes a SQL identifier, which cannot be
bound as a parameter: an exhaustive match is the only form that is both injection-proof
and verifiable by reading.

Short on purpose. Both variants are backed by a non-null column, which is what lets a
cursor locate a position unambiguously; ordering by a nullable one — year, rating —
additionally needs the cursor to encode absence and the null position to be pinned.

fields.description:
Monotonic counter that advances whenever the library's contents change.

A string rather than an `Int` because the value exceeds 32 bits, which is the width

What was added to this library most recently, newest first.

For a film library, its films by date added. For a series library, new episodes
grouped as the reference groups them: a batch of episodes added within twenty hours
of one another stands for its season, or its series when it spans several seasons,
and a lone episode for itself; each item appears once, at its newest batch. So the
list mixes series, seasons and episodes.

Pages forward only: the grouping is computed from the newest addition down, so there
is no end to page back from.

fields.name: node
fields.description:
Refetches any object by its global identifier.

The single entry point Relay clients use to refresh cached objects. Returns null when
nothing carries that identifier; a malformed identifier is an error rather than null,
because it signals a client bug rather than a deleted object.

args.name: id

fields.name: nodes
fields.description:
Refetches several objects by their global identifiers, in the order given.

The batched form of `node`. A client refreshing a screenful of cached objects would
otherwise send one query per object, or an aliased query whose *text* grows with the
request; here the count is a value. Entries are null where nothing carries that
identifier, so positions line up with the input and a missing object does not shift
the rest.

Identifiers are deduplicated before loading, so repeating one costs nothing.

fields.name: search
fields.description:
Items whose title matches a search term, across every library.

Matches a *word prefix*: `hell` finds "Good News About Hell", and accents are folded so
`soiree` finds "# Pire Soirée". A term inside a word does not match — the index is a
range scan, not a substring scan.

Polymorphic and cross-library by design: results mix films, series and episodes from
different libraries, which is what a single search box needs. Narrow with `kinds`.

Ordered by sort title. Not by relevance: ranking needs a score this server does not
compute, and a title ordering at least gives the cursor a stable position to resume
from. A blank term matches nothing rather than everything.

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type
validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution
behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally
including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing
additional information to the executor.

types.name: __DirectiveLocation
types.description:
A Directive can be adjacent to many parts of the GraphQL language, a
__DirectiveLocation describes one such possible adjacencies.

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description:
One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a
placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned
in a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Field
types.description:
Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which
has a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description:
Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an
InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and
optionally a default value.

types.name: __Schema
types.description:
A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes
all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry
points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.description:
description of __Schema for newer graphiql introspection schema
requirements

fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description:

be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description:
If this server support subscription, the type that subscription

fields.name: directives

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds
of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about
that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name and
description, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface
types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface,
provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose
other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description:
Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid
fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description:
Indicates this type is an interface. `fields` and `possibleTypes` are
valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.
